Preveza Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Preveza, Greece

Demolished. A Jewish presence existed in Preveza as early as the 16th century but disappeared until the mid-19th century, when settlers arrived from Ioannina, Arta, and Corfu; the community formally organized in 1903, reaching 200 residents by 1904. A 1908 Alliance Israelite-supported school preceded 1913 Zionist activity; population reached 250 by 1940. On March 25, 1944, Germans gathered 245 local Jews and transferred them to Arta, combining with 352 Arta Jews for transport to Agrinion, then deportation to Auschwitz on April 2 as part of the first transport from Athens. Only 17 survivors returned from hiding after the war, with numbers dwindling thereafter. This cemetery's founding is unknown, presumed 19th century, though earlier burials may have occurred on the site.
